page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Its core configuration consists of 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core via hyperthreading. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding a allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage and relies on network-attached storage solutions. Networking features a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Hardware-level acceleration features include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced single-core capability paired with modest multi-core and memory throughput. Single-threaded performance indicators, including stress-ng single-core (1876.59) and Geekbench single-core (1566.0), place the server in average benchmark distributions. Small LLM inference text generation reaches 107.71 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-core metrics sit in lower percentiles, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core scores (3865.79) and Geekbench multi-core scores (3365.0). Uncached memory read bandwidth (31.76 GB/sec) and memory write bandwidth (25.49 GB/sec) reflect standard single-channel memory limits for this tier.

The hardware configuration of the ecs.c7.xlarge provides dedicated CPU resource allocation suited for workloads requiring steady single-core execution without large memory footprints. The absence of local storage and high memory overhead yields a clear resource tradeoff favoring compute consistency over memory-intensive processing. Primary workload fits include lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch processing pipelines, web server utility roles, and basic computational tasks.
